sentences.text: Ankosh Kumar @ Teetu vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 22
March, 2023

High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 84
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 1886 of 2023
Applicant :- Ankosh Kumar @ Teetu

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Sunil Kumar,Rajesh Kumar
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Ashwini Kumar,Ganesh Shanker Srivastava
Hon'ble Nalin Kumar Srivastava,J.
This application has been moved on behalf of the applicant -Ankosh Kumar @ Teetu seeking
anticipatory bail in Case Crime No. 68 of 2021, under Sections 363, 366, 376-D, 506, I.P.C. and
Section 5/6 Pocso Act, Police Station Tirwa, District Kannauj.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State as well as learned counsel for the complainant and perused the record.

It has been argued by the learned counsel for the applicant that applicant is innocent and he has apprehension of his arrest in the above-mentioned case, whereas there is no credible evidence against him.
Allegations levelled against the applicant are false.
The investigation of the case has been completed and charge-sheet has been filed and cognizance has been taken by the Court concerned.
It has been submitted that the applicant has fully cooperated in the investigation.
He has no criminal antecedents.
In case, applicant is granted anticipatory bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and would obey all conditions of bail.
Learned A.G.A. and learned counsel for the complainant opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail.

sentences.text: It is alleged in the F.I.R. that the minor victim of the case while going to temple with her mother and sister was abducted by the present accused-applicant along with other two accused persons in four wheeler vehicle and on gun point, she was raped by the accused-persons and subsequently, they left her near the D.N. College and fled away threatening her for life.

She informed about the incident dated 3.1.2021 to her mother and sister and went to the police station to lodge FIR but the same was not registered and ultimately by order of the Court, the FIR was lodged and that it appears to be a reason for delayed FIR and for the same reason, the minor victim has been medically examined on 22.3.2021.
In the medical examination, the age of the victim is ascertained about 18 years, whereas no sign of sexual assault was found.

In her statement recorded under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C., the prosecution version has been corroborated by the minor victim and specific role in the commission of rape has been assigned to the present accused-applicant.

It also reveals from the record that on 2.1.2021, the mother of the victim Smt. Premlata moved a complaint to Superintendent of Police, Auraiya alleging therein that the present accused often teases her daughter and he also tried to outrage her modesty by entering into her house on 22.12.2020.

On the said complaint, on the direction of the Superintendent of Police, Auraiya, an inquiry was made by the police and on 8.1.2021, the inquiry report by S.I.
Mukesh Kumar was filed, wherein it was mentioned that during the investigation, it was found that the allegations made against the accused Ankosh Kumar @ Teetu are completely false and in fact there was some altercation between both the parties on account of a phone call made by some unknown persons, however, that phone call was not made by accused Ankosh Kumar @ Teetu.
It belonged to some Vivek Rajput resident of Kanpur.

The contention of the learned counsel for the applicant that while the inquiry regarding alleged incident of 22.12.2020 was pending, the victim or his family member could very well inform the Investigating Officer about the present incident because inquiry report had been filed till then but nothing was done by them and as per FIR of this case on 19.1.2021, a registered application to Superintendent of Police, Kannauj was sent by the victim, which cannot get weightage at this stage because the mental agony of the family of the minor victim who has been raped by three persons may very well be understood.
The FIR further indicates that after the incident, the family of the victim tried to approach the police and they went to Police Station, Tirwa but no report was lodged.

So far as, the factum of summoning the accused in the matter is concerned, the order passed by the POCSO Court, Kannauj on 13.10.2022, may be taken into account, whereby the protest petition filed by the victim was accepted by the Court and while rejecting the final report submitted by the I.O.,
the present accused-applicant along with other two accused-persons was summoned under Sections 363, 366, 376-D, 506 I.P.C. and Section 5/6 POCSO Act and the cognizance was taken under Section 190(1) (b) Cr.P.C. by the Court.
This is a case of gang rape committed to the minor victim.
In the facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is not inclined to grant any anticipatory bail to the present accused-applicant.
Accordingly, the present anticipatory bail application is rejected.
